title: King and rook against king
line: The box that shrinks, and the opposition for the final check.

steps.text: King and rook against a lone king always wins. The rook builds a wall the king cannot cross, and your king pushes it back.
Build the wall: put the rook on the row between the two kings, far from the black king.
steps.hint: The black king stands on the fifth row. The rook goes one row below it.
steps.after: The black king is in a box: it cannot cross the rook's row.

steps.text: Bring your king up. When the black king steps back, move the rook up behind it. Keep the rook far from the black king.
On the edge, the kings stand face to face with one square between them. This is the opposition. Now a rook check is mate.
steps.hint: Check along the edge. Your king covers the squares in front of the black king.
steps.after: Checkmate. The rook holds the edge, and your king takes the three squares in front of the black king.

steps.text: Here the kings do not face each other, so a check is not mate. Make a waiting move: slide the rook along its row.

also.a7c7: That waits too. This lesson goes on with the rook one square along.
also.a7d7: That waits too. This lesson goes on with the rook one square along.

wrong.a7g7: The king takes the rook, and with a king alone you cannot mate. Keep the rook far from the black king.

steps.hint: Keep the rook on its row, far from the black king.
steps.after: Black must move. It goes toward the corner, away from your king.

steps.text: Follow the black king with yours, one step toward the corner.
steps.hint: Your king steps along its row toward the black king.
steps.after: The black king steps into the corner.

steps.text: Step closer again, but leave Black a move. A rook or king move that takes every square without check is stalemate.

wrong.b7g7: That is stalemate: Black is not in check and has no legal move. The game is a draw.

steps.hint: Your king steps along its row once more.
steps.after: Black's only move is back out of the corner, in front of your king.

steps.text: The kings face each other. Mate on the edge.
steps.hint: The rook checks along the back row.

summary: Wall the king in with the rook, shrink the box, then check on the edge when the kings face each other.
